phase3_findings.description: docs/external/rule-sets.md line 5 (changed by this PR) implies [[rls]] only applies one fixed filter to every request; the Row-Level Security guide (lines 26, 70) documents dynamic per-request rules from _meta, so operators may wrongly conclude per-user row scoping needs rule sets.
docs/external/row-level-security.md line 172 describes rule sets as limiting only tables and columns; it no longer mentions row rules.
CompiledRule does not enforce slots/tables consistency with condition at construction and holds a mutable sqlglot tree in a frozen dataclass.
GuardSpec.tables is a plain dict beside a MappingProxyType; LoadedRuleSets.compiled is public and defaults empty, allowing row rules with nothing compiled (caught at use time).
ReferencedByRule stores two variants as independent optional fields kept consistent only by a validator; downstream `or ""` fallbacks could yield empty identifiers if bypassed.
_Compiler keeps per-compile state on an instance reused across tables.
No test covers the duplicate base-alias-index refusal in _proven_scoped_tables.
guard_spec RuntimeError tested only with every set's compiled rules cleared, not a single table's.

report:
## Verdict: REJECT (one Important documentation finding at the important threshold)
This PR is not ready to merge, because one sentence the PR changed in the published rule-sets guide tells operators that Row-Level Security only filters rows the same way for every request, which is not true.
Rule applied: rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `docs/external/rule-sets.md` line 5 now says "If you only need to narrow answers to certain rows for every request alike, read Row-Level Security instead." This suggests that `[[rls]]` rules only apply one fixed filter to every request. The Row-Level Security guide (`docs/external/row-level-security.md` lines 26 and 70) describes dynamic rules that read a value from each request's `_meta` to limit answers to the requesting user. An operator who reads this sentence could wrongly think per-user row filtering needs rule sets. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: published doc page under docs/external; no tool or agent-instruction file reads it; fixing the sentence changes no output -->

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (8)

<details><summary>8 items</summary>

1. `docs/external/row-level-security.md` line 172 says per-role rule sets limit each request to the tables and columns one role may read. With this change, rule sets also limit rows through `row_rule`, and the sentence does not mention that. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 512-538: `CompiledRule` does not check at construction that `slots` and `tables` match its `condition`. It holds a mutable sqlglot tree inside a frozen dataclass. Its one producer and the load-time proof keep it correct today. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 644-699: `GuardSpec.tables` is a plain `dict` while `rules` is a `MappingProxyType`. `LoadedRuleSets.compiled` is public and defaults to empty, so a value with row rules and nothing compiled can exist. `guard_spec` catches that at use time with a `RuntimeError`, which the guard turns into a refusal. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 271-292: `ReferencedByRule` stores its two variants as three independent optional fields, kept consistent only by a validator. The compiler and checks then write `node.source_column or ""`, which would produce an empty identifier if the validator were bypassed. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 541-561: `_Compiler` keeps per-compile state (`_slots`, `_tables`) on an instance that is reused for every table in a set. This is correct only while calls stay sequential and never nest. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 518-519: no test covers the refusal in `_proven_scoped_tables` when two derived tables use the same base alias index. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 695-698: the test for `guard_spec`'s `RuntimeError` clears every set's compiled rules. No test drops a single table's compiled rule while its sibling tables stay compiled. (raised by 1/6 agents)
- VC-17: FAIL (suggestion) — The internal doc asserts any exception while building or proving the filter is refused with KIND_UNCHECKED and text naming no table or column. [docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Doc line 104 of docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md says any exception while building or proving the filter is refused 'the same way' (KIND_UNCHECKED), with text naming no table or column. Text part holds: RuleSetRefusal.__init__ (rule_sets.py:203-207) passes only REFUSAL_PREFIX+kind to the exception message, detail (which may name tables) is log-only; RefusalRedactingRunner.run_sql (1002-1004) re-raises RuleSetRefusal unchanged, so str(exc) carries only the kind. A TypeError from _scoped_body/CompiledRule.instantiate is caught by `except Exception` in RuleSetGuardRunner.run_sql (886-893) and becomes RuleSetRefusal(KIND_UNCHECKED); that part holds. Counterexample to 'refused the same way': _rename_ctes (called at 820 during apply_rule_set, before building the filters) raises RuleSetRefusal(KIND_UNSUPPORTED, ...) at 397; run_sql's `except RuleSetRefusal: raise` (879-885) passes it through with KIND_UNSUPPORTED, not KIND_UNCHECKED. Also any other RuleSetRefusal kind raised in the build path is not UNCHECKED. So the absolute 'any exception ... same way' wording is inaccurate; only unexpected non-RuleSetRefusal exceptions and the re-walk refusals map to KIND_UNCHECKED. The path is likely defensive, so impact is wording only.

  </details>

</details>

[src/sqllens/rule_sets.py]

  Read CompiledRule.instantiate (src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:526-538) and the compiler (:461-610): every Column is built via _slot_column with a quoted slot identifier as table, every TableAlias via _exists with a slot identifier, and the only Placeholder constructed is exp.Placeholder(this='user_id'); all slot names come from _slot_name(0..slots-1), so names[...] lookups match the aliases mapping when len(aliases)==slots (checked at :527). The claim's remaining dependency part (sqlglot's exp.Column.table returning the qualifier name, exp.TableAlias.name returning the alias identifier) needs sqlglot's expressions.py, but the item has no dependency_sources and neither view contains sqlglot source (Glob of the review dir for sqlglot/expressions* found nothing). [src/sqllens/rule_sets.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

The item supplies no dependency_sources, and sqlglot is not in the views, so the library behavior is unverified. I did not read any sqlglot parser.py, and I did not run prove_compiled_rule or a parse of '-5'.

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

The repo code was read: rule_sets.py:277-282 (_is_cte_reference checks table.name in scope.cte_sources with no db/catalog) and :379-402 (_rename_ctes uses scope.cte_sources[table.name].expression, takes it as the CTE or its find_ancestor(exp.CTE), and refuses with RuleSetRefusal if no CTE is found or it is not in the collected CTE ids). So the code does rely on the assumption, and fails closed when it does not hold. Whether sqlglot builds cte_sources keyed by name with Scope/Table values whose expression is the CTE or has a CTE ancestor, for recursive and nested WITH, could not be settled from the permitted sources. I did not read sqlglot optimizer/scope.py (_traverse_ctes at around line 871) under an authorised dependency directory. Missing evidence: sqlglot scope.py supplied via dependency_sources, or a run of nested and recursive WITH queries through traverse_scope.

[tests/unit/test_row_rules.py:150]

Not settled: the literal message strings ('Unable to extract tag using discriminator', 'does not match any of the expected tags', 'at least 1 item') live in the compiled pydantic_core 2.50.4 Rust extension (pydantic 2.14.3 in .venv); core_schema.py only lists the error type names (union_tag_not_found, union_tag_invalid, too_short, lines 4923-4985). A Grep of site-packages found no text match, and I did not run the tests or a pydantic snippet to see the output. These strings match my recollection of pydantic v2 but that is not source evidence.

- VC-46: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — Under the example set as user 7, with an order hidden from user 7 whose `total` is 100 and every visible order's `total` at most 9, `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.total * 1000000000000000000 > 0` returns the number of visible orders without an error; the same statement under a confirmed set that lists `orders` with no row rule fails with MySQL error 1690. [tests/connectors/test_row_rules_mysql.py:280-292]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Criteria file read; criterion 9 present and counted. The head view has a test matching the criterion: tests/connectors/test_row_rules_mysql.py:280-292 (test_a_model_expression_never_runs_on_a_hidden_row) runs the overflow SQL under the example set for user 7 and expects count 2, then under a set listing orders with no row rule and expects error.args[0] == 1690. Fixture data (lines 100-104) has hidden order 14 with total 100 and visible orders 10 and 15 with totals 5 and 8. The claim depends on MySQL actually evaluating the LIMIT-materialized derived table before the model's WHERE and on MySQL raising 1690 for the unscoped case. Reading the source cannot settle that. I did not run the live-MySQL test: pytest tests/connectors/test_row_rules_mysql.py -k never_runs_on_a_hidden_row. Trigger-alternative splitting was not completed for the same reason.

  </details>

- VC-47: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — Under the example set, on a server with MySQL's default `optimizer_switch`, MySQL's `EXPLAIN` of the SQL the guard produces for `SELECT c.name, o.total, cu.code FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id JOIN currencies cu ON cu.id = 1` shows the derived tables for `customers` and `orders` as materialized (`select_type` `DERIVED`) and no materialized derived table for `currencies`. So each reference to a table with a row rule is built in full, with every row its rule leaves visible, before the model's own conditions apply, and that work counts against the statement timeout; a table without a row rule stays mergeable. [diff.patch]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json is a valid list of {criterion,text} objects and carries criterion 10, so it counts. The diff adds _scoped_body (diff.patch ~1157-1174), which builds SELECT <cols> FROM t AS sl.. WHERE <rule> LIMIT 18446744073709551615, with a comment saying the LIMIT stops MySQL merging the derived table. The diff also adds test_explain_shows_scoped_tables_materialized_and_unscoped_mergeable (diff.patch ~1682-1702), which runs EXPLAIN on exactly the claimed query and asserts DERIVED rows for sl0_0_0 and sl0_1_0 and a non-DERIVED row for rr_currencies. The claim is about what a live MySQL server's EXPLAIN reports, and that is a runtime result. I did not run that EXPLAIN or the test, and no recorded test output was supplied. The source trace is consistent with the claim, because a LIMIT derived table is not merged. It does not settle the exact EXPLAIN rows or the unscoped table's shape. Command not run: the MySQL-backed test test_explain_shows_scoped_tables_materialized_and_unscoped_mergeable.

  </details>

</details>

The path is likely defensive, so impact is wording only.
